# Volume 5 — CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“This is just the sort of day you feel as if things might happen,” stated Grace, reacting to the attraction of blue hills and clear air. She squeezed herself with joy and performed a hornpipe atop the bench tombstone belonging to old Hezekiah Pollock, greatly horrifying a pair of elderly maidens who chanced to drive by at the exact moment Grace balanced on a single foot around the marker, shaking her remaining foot along with her arms up in the air.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0000 }

“And that,” an elderly maiden moaned, “is the daughter of our minister.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0001 }

“What else could one anticipate from the household of a widower?” the second elderly spinster moaned. Thereupon, both of them wagged their heads.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0002 }

The Ashdowns were outside in the damp morning air early on Saturday, enjoying a wonderful awareness of their day off. They never possessed any duties on a holiday. Even though Bess and Izzy Carrow were required to perform specific chores around the house on Saturday mornings, the daughters of the manse possessed the freedom to wander from dawn until nightfall if they desired. Grace enjoyed this, but Ida experienced a hidden, painful shame over the fact that they were never taught any skills. Cooking, sewing, and knitting were manageable for the remaining girls in her school class; only she was a small dunce.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0003 }

It was proposed by Tobias that they embark on an exploration; consequently, they made their way unhurriedly across the fir grove, collecting Rupert as they went, who was kneeling within the wet grass to examine his beloved ants. Past the grove, they emerged into the pasture field belonging to Mr. Taylor, which was dotted throughout with the pale remnants of dandelions; situated in a distant corner stood an ancient, dilapidated barn, in which Mr. Taylor occasionally kept his extra harvest of hay, though it served no additional function whatsoever. To that place the Ashdown children marched, and they searched around the lower level for a number of minutes.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0004 }

“What was that?” Ida abruptly murmured.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0005 }

The group paid attention. From the hayloft overhead, a soft yet clear rustling sound emerged. A glance passed between the Ashdowns.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0006 }

“An object is present up in that location,” Grace whispered softly.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0007 }

“I will go up to find out what is there,” Tobias said with determination.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0008 }

“Oh, please refrain,” Ida implored, grasping his arm.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0009 }

“I’m departing.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0010 }

“Then we will all go along, as well,” Grace stated.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0011 }

All four of them scaled the rickety ladder; while Tobias and Grace were entirely fearless, Ida was drained of color by terror, and Rupert mused somewhat distantly about whether they might discover a bat in the loft above. He desperately wished to observe a bat during the daytime.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0012 }

As soon as they descended from the ladder, the source of the rustling sound became visible to them, and the vision left them speechless for a short time.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0013 }

Folded up within a small nook in the hay, a girl appeared to have only recently woken up. As her eyes fell upon them, she rose to her feet, appearing somewhat unsteady, and inside the brilliant sunshine pouring through the cobweb-covered window at her back, her slender, sun-browned face was revealed to be extremely pale beneath its brownness. Pairings of limp, heavy, flaxen-colored braids hung on her, and her eyes were most unusual—“white eyes,” as they appeared to the manse children, while her gaze toward them was part rebellious, part sorrowful. Their shade of blue was actually so faint that an appearance of near-whiteness was created, particularly in comparison to the thin black circle that bordered each iris. Wearing neither shoes nor head covering, she was dressed in an old, threadbare, frayed tartan garment that was far too brief and constricted for her frame. Regarding her age, her shriveled small face made it possible for her to be nearly any number of years old, though her stature appeared to place her around twelve.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0014 }

“Who are you?” inquired Tobias.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0015 }

The girl cast her eyes around, appearing to search for a path to flee. Following that, she appeared to surrender, letting out a slight tremble of hopelessness.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0016 }

“My name is Mary Stubbs,” she declared.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0017 }

“Where did you arrive from?” Tobias asked further.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0018 }

Mary, rather than answering, abruptly dropped or collapsed onto the hay and started weeping. Grace immediately threw herself down at her side, wrapping her arm around the slender, trembling shoulders.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0019 }

“You cease troubling her,” she ordered Tobias. She subsequently embraced the waif. “Don’t weep, dear. Simply inform us what is wrong. We are friends.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0020 }

“My hunger is—so—terrible,” cried Mary. “Since Thursday morning, nothing has passed my lips, ‘save for some brook water from outside.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0021 }

The kids from the manse stared at one another, filled with horror. Grace jumped to her feet.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0022 }

“You come straight up to the manse and have a bite to eat prior to saying another word.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0023 }

Mary drew back.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0024 }

“Oh—I am unable to. What reaction will your pa and ma have? Additionally, I would be sent back by them.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0025 }

“We are without a mother, and you will not be a concern to father. Aunt Martha will not care either. Come along, I tell you.” Grace struck her foot against the ground with impatience. Could this strange girl be determined to die of hunger practically on their doorstep?
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0026 }

Mary gave in. Her weakness was such that descending the ladder was a great struggle, yet somehow she was assisted down, across the field, and into the kitchen of the manse. Aunt Martha, busy with her Saturday cooking chores, paid her no attention. Grace and Ida rushed to the pantry and searched it thoroughly for whatever food was inside—a bit of “ditto,” bread, butter, milk, and a pie of questionable quality. Mary Stubbs devoured the nourishment eagerly and without complaint, while the children of the manse gathered around to observe her. Tobias observed that her mouth was pretty and her teeth were very nice, even, and white. Grace concluded, with hidden dread, that Mary wore nothing at all beneath that tattered, bleached dress. Ida felt complete compassion, Rupert experienced entertained astonishment, and every one of them was filled with curiosity.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0027 }

“Now step out to the churchyard and inform us concerning yourself,” commanded Grace, as Mary’s hunger began to diminish. Mary was by this time entirely willing. Her innate liveliness had been renewed by the meal, which set free her tongue that was not at all disinclined to speak.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0028 }

“You won’t tell your pa or anybody if I tell you?” she demanded, once she had taken her seat atop the gravestone of Mr. Pollock. Facing her on a different stone, the children from the manse formed a row. Flavor, secrecy, and excitement were present here. An event had taken place.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0029 }

“No, we shall not.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0030 }

“Cross your hearts?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0031 }

“Cross our hearts.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0032 }

“Indeed, I have escaped. Mrs. Grimble was housing me across the harbor. Are you acquainted with Mrs. Grimble?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0033 }

“No.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0034 }

“Well, knowing her isn't something you want. An awful woman is what she is. My, I hate her so much! I was worked to death by her and she refused to give me half enough to eat, plus ‘most every day she used to larrup me. Look a-here.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0035 }

Mary turned up the tattered sleeves she wore, revealing her bony arms alongside slender hands that were cracked and sore from the cold. Dark bruises covered them completely. A shudder passed through the manse children. Deep anger brought a bright red flush to Grace's face. Ida's eyes, blue in color, brimmed with tears.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0036 }

“On Wednesday night, she hit me using a stick,” Mary said, uncaringly. “That happened because I permitted the cow to knock a milk pail over. How could I have known the stupid old cow would kick?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0037 }

Her audience experienced a sensation that was not entirely disagreeable. Although they would not think of employing such questionable terms themselves, hearing another person utter them—especially a girl—was quite stimulating. Without a doubt, this Mary Stubbs was a fascinating individual.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0038 }

“You running away isn’t something I blame you for,” Grace said.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0039 }

“Oh, her beating me wasn't the reason I took off. Getting beaten was just a normal part of my everyday life. It happened so often I was completely accustomed to it. No, my plan to run away had been set for seven days because it came to my attention that Mrs. Grimble intended to lease her land, relocate her home to Kettlebridge, and hand me over to one of her cousins up near Port Marlow. That was something I refused to put up with. Her character was far nastier than Mrs. Grimble’s. During the previous summer, Mrs. Grimble let her have me for thirty days, and I would prefer the devil's own company.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0040 }

The second sensation occurred, yet Ida appeared uncertain.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0041 }

“So I resolved to clear out. I possessed seventy cents I had put aside, which Mrs. John Crawford bestowed on me back in the spring because I planted potatoes on her behalf. Mrs. Grimble was unaware of it. She happened to be away calling on her cousin at the time I planted them. My plan was to slip up here to the Glen, purchase a ticket bound for Port Marlow, and attempt to find employment in that place. I am a hard worker, I can assure you. There is not one lazy bone anywhere in my body. Therefore, I took off Thursday morning before Mrs. Grimble had risen and made my way on foot to the Glen—a distance of six miles. But upon arriving at the station, I discovered that my money was lost. I don't know how—I don't know where. At any rate, it had vanished. I was at a loss for what to do. Had I returned to old Lady Grimble, she would have skinning me alive. Consequently, I departed and concealed myself inside that old barn.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0042 }

“And what are you going to do at this point?” Tobias inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0043 }

“I am uncertain. It seems I must return and accept the consequences. My ability to endure it has likely improved now that I have eaten something.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0044 }

Yet, hidden beneath the bold exterior, terror lingered in the eyes of Mary. Moving swiftly from the first headstone to the next, Ida wrapped an arm around Mary.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0045 }

“Refrain from returning. Merely remain here alongside us.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0046 }

“Oh, Mrs. Grimble’ll track me down,” Mary stated. “She’s probably searching for me already. Provided your family doesn't object, I guess I could remain right here until she discovers my location. Thinking I could run away was completely foolish of me. Even a weasel couldn't escape her. However, my misery was just so great.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0047 }

Mary had a tremble in her voice, yet she felt embarrassment over revealing her frailty.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0048 }

“For the past four years, my existence has been worse than a dog’s,” she declared in a tone of defiance.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0049 }

“Has it been four years that you’ve spent with Mrs. Grimble?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0050 }

“Yip. I was eight years old when she removed me from the asylum located in Hopetown.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0051 }

“Mrs. Carrow originated from that very location,” Grace blurted out.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0052 }

“For two years, I remained in the asylum, having been placed in that institution at six years old. My mother had hanged herself, while my father had slit his own throat.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0053 }

“Holy cats! Why?” asked Tobias.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0054 }

“Alcohol,” Mary stated concisely.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0055 }

“And you do not have any relatives?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0056 }

“There isn’t a single one that I’m aware of. However, there had to be some at one time. I received my names from six of them. Mary Martha Lucilla Vane Ball Stubbs is my complete name. Is it possible to top that? A wealthy man was my grandfather. It’s my bet that his wealth exceeded your grandfather’s. Yet it was all guzzled away by pa, and ma contributed her share as well. Furthermore, they were accustomed to striking me. Goodness, I’ve received so many thrashings that I somewhat enjoy it.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0057 }

Mary jerked her head back. Sensing that the children from the manse felt pity toward her because of her numerous lashings, she rejected their pity. What she desired was their envy. She glanced around herself with a cheerful air. Since the lethargy brought on by hunger had vanished from them, her unusual eyes sparkled with brightness. It was her intention to demonstrate to those youths precisely how important a figure she truly was.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0058 }

“I have been ill a tremendous amount,” she declared boastfully. “Only a few children would be able to survive all that I survived. Scarlet fever, measles, ersipelas, mumps, whooping cough, and pewmonia have all afflicted me.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0059 }

“Have you ever been sick to the point of death?” Ida inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0060 }

“I am not certain,” Mary uttered with hesitation.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0061 }

“Naturally she was not,” mocked Tobias. “You perish when you are terminally ill.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0062 }

“Oh, well, I didn't actually pass away,” Mary stated, “yet I was extremely close to it on one occasion. My death was assumed by them, and my preparation for burial was underway when I suddenly revived.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0063 }

“How does it feel when someone is half dead?” Tobias inquired with curiosity.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0064 }

“As if it were nothing. Days went by before I realized it. It happened during my bout of pewmonia. Mrs. Grimble refused to call a doctor—stating she had no intention of incurring that kind of cost for a home girl. Nursing me with poultices, old Aunt Christina MacAllister was the one who cared for me. She brought me back to health. Yet at times I wish the remaining half of me had simply died to end it all. My situation would have been better.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0065 }

“I guess you would if you were to go to heaven,” Grace said, with a good deal of doubt.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0066 }

“Well, where else can one possibly go?” Mary asked, sounding bewildered.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0067 }

“You know, hell exists,” whispered Ida, drawing Mary close to soften the impact of the grim thought.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0068 }

“What is that, Hell?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0069 }

“Indeed, the devil makes his home there,” Tobias declared. “He is familiar to you—you made mention of him.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0070 }

“Oh, certainly, but I was unaware that he possessed a residence anywhere. My belief was that he merely wandered about. When he was living, Mr. Grimble would bring up hell. He was forever advising people to travel to that location. I assumed it was a certain spot across in New Brunswick, which was his place of origin.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0071 }

“An atrocious location is hell,” Grace declared, experiencing the theatrical pleasure arising from the narration of terrible matters. “Upon dying, wicked individuals travel to that realm where they undergo eternal combustion in flames.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0072 }

“Who gave you that information?” Mary asked, unable to believe it.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0073 }

“It is located within the Bible. Furthermore, Mr. Isaac Crothers at Juneford informed us of it as well during Sunday School. Being an elder alongside a pillar of the church, he possessed complete knowledge regarding it. However, there is no need for you to be anxious. Provided that you behave well, your destination will be heaven, whereas if your behavior is bad, my assumption is that hell would be your preferred destination.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0074 }

“I wouldn’t,” Mary stated emphatically. “Regardless of how wicked I was I wouldn’t wish to be burned over and over. I am aware of how it feels. A red hot poker was picked up by me once by mistake. What is required of one to be good?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0075 }

“You have to attend church and Sunday School, read the Bible, say your prayers every night, and donate to missions,” Ida stated.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0076 }

“That seems like a tall request,” Mary remarked. “Is there anything more?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0077 }

“You are required to pray to God for pardon regarding the transgressions you have done.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0078 }

“However, I have not ever com—committed a single one,” Mary stated. “In any case, what constitutes a sin?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0079 }

“Oh, Mary, it is impossible that you haven't. All people do. Was there never a time you uttered a falsehood?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0080 }

“Quantities of them,” Mary stated.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0081 }

“Such a terrible sin,” Ida stated with gravity.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0082 }

“Are you saying,” Mary asked, “that committing a falsehood occasionally would cause me to be damned? Truly, I was forced to. Had I not uttered an untruth to Mr. Grimble on one occasion, he would have shattered all the bones in my frame. Spoken falsehoods have spared me numerous beatings, I assure you.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0083 }

Ida let out a sigh. Resolving such an abundance of problems was beyond her capabilities. The thought of receiving a harsh flogging made her tremble. It was quite probable that she would have been dishonest as well. She held Mary’s small, rough hand in a tight grip.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0084 }

“Do you have no other dress besides that one?” inquired Grace, a person whose cheerful temperament declined to brood over unpleasant matters.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0085 }

“I only wore this dress since it had no value,” exclaimed Mary with a blush. “My garments had been purchased by Mrs. Grimble, and I refused to owe her for a single thing. Furthermore, I am truthful. Had I intended to flee, I had no intention of taking any of her possessions that possessed real worth. Once I am grown, I shall own a blue sating dress. Your personal attire does not appear particularly fashionable. I assumed the offspring of ministers were perpetually clad in fine clothes.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0086 }

That Mary possessed a temper and had sensitive spots was obvious. Nevertheless, her strange, wild allure enchanted everyone. That afternoon, she was brought to Fern Hollow and presented to the Carrows as “a friend of ours from over-harbour who is visiting us.” The Carrows received her without question, possibly owing to the fact that she appeared reasonably respectable by then. Following dinner—during which Aunt Martha had muttered and Mr. Ashdown had remained half-unconscious while contemplating his Sunday sermon—Grace had persuaded Mary to wear one of her dresses, along with various other garments. Her hair being tidily braided, Mary proved acceptable enough. Because she was familiar with a number of novel and thrilling games, and because her speech was not without zest, she made a satisfactory playmate. Indeed, a few of her remarks caused Bess and Izzy to view her somewhat suspiciously. Although they were uncertain about how their mother would have viewed her, they were entirely certain of Tabitha’s opinion. Still, since she was a guest at the manse, she had to be fine.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0087 }

As the time for sleep arrived, deciding where Mary ought to lie down presented a difficulty.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0088 }

“You know we are unable to place her in the guest room,” Grace remarked to Ida in a state of perplexity.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0089 }

“There isn’t anything in my head,” Mary exclaimed, sounding hurt.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0090 }

“Oh, I did not intend to imply that,” Grace objected. “Everything in the spare room is in complete disarray. A large hole was chewed into the feather tick by mice so they could build a nest inside it. It remained completely undiscovered by us until Aunt Martha assigned the room to the Rev. Mr. Fisher from Port Marlow when he stayed overnight last week. It did not take him long to discover it. Consequently, father was forced to surrender his own bed to him and spend the night on the study lounge instead. According to Aunt Martha, she has not yet found the time required to repair the bed in the spare room; therefore, it remains unusable for anyone to sleep in, regardless of how clean their head might be. Furthermore, our room is extremely tiny, and the bed itself is so small that there is no space for you to share it with us.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0091 }

“If a quilt could be lent to me, returning to the old barn’s hay for the evening is fine with me,” Mary remarked pragmatically. “Although last night possessed a bit of a chill, I have slept in worse places, setting that aside.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0092 }

“Oh, no, no, you must not do that,” Ida said. “Grace, I have conceived a scheme. Do you recall that small trestle bed located in the garret room, which has the old mattress upon it that was left there by the previous minister? Let us carry the bedclothes from the spare room upstairs and prepare Mary a bed on it. Mary, you will not object to sleeping in the garret, will you? It is situated directly over our room.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0093 }

“Any place will work for me. Lord knows, I have not possessed a respectable location for sleeping during my entire existence. My sleeping spot was situated in the loft above the kitchen at Mrs. Grimble’s. Rain seeped through the roof throughout the summer, and snow blew inside during the winter. A straw tick placed on the floor served as my bed. You will not catch me being the least bit particular regarding my sleeping quarters.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0094 }

The attic of the parsonage was an elongated, low-ceilinged, dim room, featuring a partition at one gable end. In this section, a bed was prepared for Mary with the refined hemstitched sheets and needleworked coverlet that Cecilia Ashdown had formerly crafted with such pride for her guest room, and which had managed to endure the erratic laundering of Aunt Martha. After the good nights were spoken, quiet descended upon the parsonage. Ida was on the verge of drifting off when a noise from the chamber directly overhead caused her to sit upright abruptly.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0095 }

“Listen, Grace—Mary’s crying,” she murmured in a low voice. Grace made no answer, having fallen asleep already. Ida stepped from the bed, moving in her small white gown along the hallway and ascending the garret steps. Her approach was loudly announced by the creaking floorboards, and upon arriving at the corner room, she found complete, moonlit quiet, with the trestle bed displaying merely a mound at its center.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0096 }

“Mary,” Ida murmured.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0097 }

No reply was made.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0098 }

Ida moved quietly near the bed and tugged on the coverlet. “Mary, I know you are crying. I heard you. Are you lonesome?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0099 }

Mary unexpectedly came into sight, yet she uttered no words.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0100 }

“Allow me to join you in there. I feel cold,” uttered Ida, who was trembling in the brisk draft, because the small attic window stood unclosed, letting in the sharp nocturnal air from the north shore.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0101 }

Mary shifted her position, allowing Ida to nestle close beside her.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0102 }

“At present you will not be lonely. It was wrong of us to leave you in this place by yourself on that initial evening.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0103 }

“I didn’t feel lonely,” Mary sniffled.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0104 }

“Why were you weeping at that moment, in that case?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0105 }

“Oh, as I sat by myself in this place, my mind simply started dwelling on matters. My thoughts turned to the necessity of returning to Mrs. Grimble—along with receiving a beating because I ran off—and—and—and facing damnation in hell on account of lying. The whole business distressed me terribly.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0106 }

“Oh, Mary,” Ida uttered, deeply upset. “I am sure God will not condemn you to hell for telling falsehoods when you were unaware that it was bad. He would not be able to. After all, He is compassionate and benevolent. Naturally, now that you realize it is wrong, you must not say any more.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0107 }

“What will happen to me if I am not allowed to tell lies?” Mary asked, sobbing. “You fail to comprehend. You are completely ignorant about it. You possess a home and a gentle father—even if I feel he is only half-present. Regardless, he does not beat you, and you receive sufficient food, such as it is—even though your old aunt is clueless regarding cookery. Indeed, today marks the very first time in my memory that I have felt as if I had eaten enough. Throughout my whole life, I have been battered around, save for those two years spent at the asylum. I was not beaten there and it proved tolerable, even if the matron was ill-tempered. She constantly appeared prepared to bite my head off a nail. However, Mrs. Grimble is an absolute nightmare, that is her true nature, and the mere thought of returning to her leaves me utterly terrified.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0108 }

“It is possible that you will not be required to do so. It is possible that we can discover a means of escape. May we both pray that God prevents you from being forced to return to Mrs. Grimble. Mary, do you offer up your prayers?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0109 }

“Oh, yes, I always repeat an old verse ‘fore I get in bed,” Mary said casually. “Though I never considered requesting any specific thing. No one on this earth ever concerned themselves with me, so I didn’t think God would either. Because you’re the daughter of a minister, He may take greater pains for you.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0110 }

“He would go to just as much effort on your behalf, Mary, I am certain,” Ida declared. “The identity of your parents is irrelevant. Simply make your request to Him—and I shall do so as well.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0111 }

“Very well,” Mary assented. “There’s no harm in it, even if it yields little benefit. Were you as acquainted with Mrs. Grimble as I am, you’d doubt that God would desire to interfere with her. Regardless, I’ll weep no further over this. It’s vastly superior to yesterday evening down inside that ancient barn, where mice were scurrying around. Observe the Seven Gulls light. Isn’t it lovely?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0112 }

“We are only able to view it from this particular window,” Ida stated. “Watching it brings me so much joy.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0113 }

“Is that so? Me as well. From the loft at Grimble, I was able to spot it, and it offered me my sole consolation. Whenever I was aching all over after getting beaten, watching it allowed me to ignore the painful spots. My thoughts would turn to the vessels journeying farther and farther from it, and I desired to be aboard one, traveling to a distant place as well—far from all of this. During winter evenings when its light was absent, I simply experienced true loneliness. Tell me, Ida, why are all of you people so good to me given that I am merely an outsider?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0114 }

“Because being so is correct. We are instructed by the Bible to show kindness toward everyone.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0115 }

“Is that so? Well, it seems to me that the majority of people do not care about it very much. I cannot recall a single person ever treating me with kindness previously—upon my life, I cannot. Tell me, Ida, are not those wall shadows lovely? They appear exactly like a group of tiny fluttery birds. And listen, Ida, I am fond of all your family as well as those Carrow boys and Izzy, but I am not fond of that Bess. She behaves in a arrogant manner.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0116 }

“Oh, no, Mary, pride isn't in her nature at all,” Ida stated with enthusiasm. “Not even a little.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0117 }

“Do not inform me. Whoever carries her head in that manner possesses pride. I dislike her.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0118 }

“She is greatly liked by all of us.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0119 }

“Oh, I guess you prefer her to me?” Mary asked with jealousy. “Is that true?”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0120 }

“Well, Mary—she has been known to us for weeks, whereas you have only been known to us for a few hours,” Ida faltered.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0121 }

“Then it is true that she is your favorite?” Mary asked furiously. “Very well! Feel whatever you want for her. It makes no difference to me. I do not need you.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0122 }

She threw her body hard up against the garret wall, causing a loud bang.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0123 }

“Oh, Mary,” uttered Ida, sliding a gentle arm across Mary’s rigid back, “do not speak in such a way. I really like you a great deal. And you cause me to feel terribly.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0124 }

There was no reply. Soon after, Ida sobbed. Immediately, Mary turned back around and wrapped Ida in a tight embrace.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0125 }

“Silence,” she commanded. “There is no need to weep about my words. My speech was as cruel as the devil himself. It would serve me right to be flayed—when all of you treat me so well. It seems to me you would prefer anybody else over me. Every beating I ever received was fully deserved. Be quiet, now. Should your tears continue, I will head straight to the harbour clad only in this night-dress and end my life in the water.”
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0126 }

Because of this frightening warning, Ida swallowed her weeping. With the lace trim from the spare-room pillow, Mary dried her tears, and the two girls nestled together once more, one granting pardon and the other receiving it, with peace re-established, observing the shadows cast by the vine leaves upon the wall in the moonlight until sleep overtook them.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0127 }

And down in the study, Rev. John Ashdown paced the room, his eyes bright and his expression entranced as he developed his sermon for the next day, completely unaware that beneath his roof resided a small, desperate spirit, tripping through obscurity and unknowingness, overwhelmed by fear and encircled by obstacles far too immense for it to handle in its unbalanced conflict against a vast, uncaring world.
{: #nw-v05-c05-p0128 }
